You are zesty_lantern63, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.

- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**

the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.

**[Download binaries](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify/releases) for Windows, Linux and macOS**

Minify is a CLI implementation of the minify [library package](https://github.com/tdewolff/minify).

## Installation
Make sure you have [Go](http://golang.org/) and [Git](http://git-scm.com/) installed.

Run the following command

    mkdir $HOME/src
    cd $HOME/src
    git clone https://github.com/tdewolff/minify.git
    cd minify
    make install

and the `minify` command will be in `$GOPATH/bin` or `$HOME/go/bin`.

If you do not have `make`, instead run the following lines to install `minify` and enable bash tab completion:

    go install ./cmd/minify
    source minify_bash_tab_completion

Optionally, you can run `go install github.com/tdewolff/minify/v2/cmd/minify@latest` to install the latest version.

### Arch Linux
Using yay, see [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/minify/)
```
yay -S minify
```

### FreeBSD
```
pkg install minify
```

### Alpine Linux
Enable the [community repo](https://wiki.alpinelinux.org/wiki/Enable_Community_Repository)
```
apk add minify
```

### MacOS
Using Homebrew, see [Brew tap](https://github.com/tdewolff/homebrew-tap/)
```
brew install tdewolff/tap/minify
```

### Debian / Ubuntu
```
sudo apt update
sudo apt install minify
```

Note: may be outdated

### Docker
Pull the image:

```
docker pull tdewolff/minify
```

> The `ENTRYPOINT` of the container is the `minify` command

and run the image, for example in interactive mode:

```bash
docker run -i tdewolff/minify sh -c 'echo "(function(){ if (a == false) { return 0; } else { return 1; } })();" | minify --type js'
```

which will output

```
(function(){return a==!1?0:1})()
```

## Usage

    Usage: minify [options] inputs...
    
    Options:
      -a, --all                   Minify all files, including hidden files and files in hidden
                                  directories
      -b, --bundle                Bundle files by concatenation into a single file
          --css-precision int     Number of significant digits to preserve in numbers, 0 is all
          --css-version int       CSS version to toggle supported optimizations (e.g. 2), by default 0 is the latest version
          --exclude []string      Path exclusion pattern, excludes paths from being processed
          --ext map[string]string
                                  Filename extension mapping to filetype (eg. css or text/css)
      -h, --help                  Help
          --html-keep-comments    Preserve all comments
          --html-keep-conditional-comments
                                  Preserve all IE conditional comments
          --html-keep-default-attrvals
                                  Preserve default attribute values
          --html-keep-document-tags
                                  Preserve html, head and body tags
          --html-keep-end-tags    Preserve all end tags
          --html-keep-quotes      Preserve quotes around attribute values
          --html-keep-whitespace  Preserve whitespace characters but still collapse multiple into one
      -i, --inplace               Minify input files in-place instead of setting output
          --include []string      Path inclusion pattern, includes paths previously excluded
          --js-keep-var-names     Preserve original variable names
          --js-precision int      Number of significant digits to preserve in numbers, 0 is all
          --js-version int        ECMAScript version to toggle supported optimizations (e.g. 2019,
                                  2020), by default 0 is the latest version
          --json-keep-numbers     Preserve original numbers instead of minifying them
          --json-precision int    Number of significant digits to preserve in numbers, 0 is all
      -l, --list                  List all accepted filetypes
          --match []string        Filename matching pattern, only matching filenames are processed
          --mime string           Mimetype (eg. text/css), optional for input filenames (DEPRECATED, use                              --type)
      -o, --output string         Output file or directory, leave blank to use stdout
      -p, --preserve []string     Preserve options (mode, ownership, timestamps, links, all)
      -q, --quiet                 Quiet mode to suppress all output
      -r, --recursive             Recursively minify directories
      -s, --sync                  Copy all files to destination directory and minify when filetype
                                  matches
          --svg-keep-comments     Preserve all comments
          --svg-precision int     Number of significant digits to preserve in numbers, 0 is all
          --type string           Filetype (eg. css or text/css), optional when specifying inputs
          --url string            URL of file to enable URL minification
      -v, --verbose               Verbose mode, set twice for more verbosity
          --version               Version
      -w, --watch                 Watch files and minify upon changes
          --xml-keep-whitespace   Preserve whitespace characters but still collapse multiple into one
    
    Arguments:
      inputs    Input files or directories, leave blank to use stdin

### Types
Default extension mapping to mimetype (and thus minifier). Use `--ext` to add more mappings, see below for an example.

	asp          text/asp
	css          text/css
	ejs          text/x-ejs-template
	gohtml       text/x-go-template
	handlebars   text/x-handlebars-template
	htm          text/html
	html         text/html
	js           application/javascript
	json         application/json
	mjs          application/javascript
	mustache     text/x-mustache-template
	php          application/x-httpd-php
	rss          application/rss+xml
	svg          image/svg+xml
	tmpl         text/x-template
	webmanifest  application/manifest+json
	xhtml        application/xhtml+xml
	xml          text/xml

## Examples
Minify **index.html** to **index-min.html**:
```sh
$ minify -o index-min.html index.html
```

Minify **index.html** to standard output (leave `-o` blank):
```sh
$ minify index.html
```

Normally the mimetype is inferred from the extension, to set the mimetype explicitly:
```sh
$ minify --type=html -o index-min.tpl index.tpl
```

You need to set the type or the mimetype option when using standard input:
```sh
$ minify --type=application/javascript < script.js > script-min.js

$ cat script.js | minify --type=js > script-min.js
```

### Directories
You can also give directories as input, and these directories can be minified recursively.

Minify files in the current working directory to **out/...** (excluding subdirectories):
```sh
$ minify -o out/ *
```

Minify files recursively in **src/...** to **out/src/...**:
```sh
$ minify -r -o out/ src
```

Minify files recursively in **src/...** to **out/...**:
```sh
$ minify -r -o out/ src/
```

Minify only javascript files in **src/**:
```sh
$ minify -r -o out/ --match=*.js src/
```

A trailing slash in the source path will copy all files inside the directory, while omitting the trainling slash will copy the directory as well. Both `src/` and `src/.` are equivalent, however `src/*` uses input expansion from bash and ignores hidden files starting with a dot.

A trailing slash in the destination path forces writing into a directory. This removes ambiguity when minifying a single file which would otherwise write to a file.

#### Map custom extensions
You can map other extensions to a minifier by using the `--ext` option, which maps a filename extension to a filetype or mimetype, which is associated with a minifier.

```sh
$ minify -r -o out/ --ext.scss=text/css --ext.xjs=js src/
```
or
```sh
$ minify -r -o out/ --ext {scss:text/css xjs:js} src/
```

#### Matching and include/exclude patterns
The patterns for `--match`, `--include`, and `--exclude` can be either a glob or a regular expression. To use the latter, prefix the pattern with `~` (if you want to use a glob starting with `~`, escape the tilde `\~...`). Match only matches the base filename, while include/exclude match the full path. Be aware of bash expansion of glob patterns, which requires you to quote the pattern or escape asterisks.

Match will filters all files by the given pattern, eg. `--match '*.css'` will only minify CSS files. The `--include` and `--exclude` options allow to add or remove certain files or directories and is interpreted in the order given. For example, `minify -rvo out/ --exclude 'src/*/**' --include 'src/foo/**' src/` will minify the directory `src/`, except for `src/*/...` where `*` is not `foo`.

You may define multiple patterns within one option, such as: `--exclude '**/folder1/**' '**/folder2/**' '**/folder3/**'` Doing this might result in unexpected behaviour when it is followed immediately by the input files, as this would be interpreted as another pattern, and not as inputs. `--exclude dir_to_exclude folder_input` Instead format accordingly: `--exclude dir_to_exclude -- folder_input`.

To match `*` or `?` literally, precede by a backslash. To specify a regular expression directly instead of a glob, use the tilde as a prefix (to use a tilde literally at the beginning, precede by a backslash). Examples of regular expressions:

```
./minify --match ~^path[0-9]/[^/]*.(js|html)$
./minify --match ~^(?i)pathCaseInsensitive[0-9]/[^/]*.(js|html)$
```

### Concatenate
When multiple inputs are given and the output is either standard output or a single file, it will concatenate the files together if you use the bundle option.

Concatenate **one.css** and **two.css** into **style.css**:
```sh
$ minify -b -o style.css one.css two.css
```

Concatenate all files in **styles/** into **style.css**:
```sh
$ minify -r -b -o style.css styles
```

You can also use `cat` as standard input to concatenate files and use gzip for example:
```sh
$ cat one.css two.css three.css | minify --type=css | gzip -9 -c > style.css.gz
```

### Watching
To watch file changes and automatically re-minify you can use the `-w` or `--watch` option.

Minify **style.css** to itself and watch changes:
```sh
$ minify -w -o style.css style.css
```

Minify and concatenate **one.css** and **two.css** to **style.css** and watch changes:
```sh
$ minify -w -o style.css one.css two.css
```

Minify files in **src/** and subdirectories to **out/** and watch changes:
```sh
$ minify -w -r -o out/ src
```

"""Conservative JavaScript tokenizer/minifier used by the CLI implementation."""
import re

_TOKEN = re.compile(r'''\s+|//[^\r\n]*|/\*[\s\S]*?\*/|(?:'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|`(?:\\.|[^`\\])*`)|(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)|(?:[$\w]+)|(?:===|!==|>>>|==|!=|<=|>=|=>|\+\+|--|&&|\|\||\?\?|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|\*\*|\.\.\.|<<|>>)''')
_WORD = re.compile(r'^[\w$]')

def minify_js(source, options=None):
    options = options or {}
    keep_names = options.get('js-keep-var-names', False)
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    while pos < len(source):
        m = _TOKEN.match(source, pos)
        if not m:
            tokens.append(source[pos]); pos += 1; continue
        t = m.group(0); pos = m.end()
        if t.isspace() or t.startswith('//') or (t.startswith('/*') and not t.startswith('/*!')):
            continue
        if t == 'true': t = '!0'
        elif t == 'false': t = '!1'
        tokens.append(t)
    out = ''
    prev = ''
    for t in tokens:
        if prev and ((_WORD.match(prev[-1:]) and _WORD.match(t[:1])) or (prev[-1:] in '+-' and t[:1] == prev[-1:]) or (prev[-1:] == '/' and t.startswith('/'))):
            out += ' '
        out += t
        prev = t
    # Safe punctuation cleanup: remove semicolons immediately before a closing brace.
    out = re.sub(r';+}', '}', out)
    # Remove a final semicolon (the parser's output convention).
    out = re.sub(r';+$', '', out)
    return out

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/html_min.py
+"""Small HTML minifier used by the minify CLI format dispatcher."""
+import re
+import html
+
+_TOKEN = re.compile(r'<!--[\s\S]*?-->|<![^>]*>|</?[^>]+>|[^<]+')
+_ATTR = re.compile(r'''([^\s=/>]+)(?:\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|([^\s>]+)))?''')
+_VOID = set('area base br col embed hr img input link meta param source track wbr'.split())
+_BLOCK = set('address article aside blockquote body dd div dl dt fieldset figcaption figure footer form h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 head header hr html li main nav ol p pre section table tbody td tfoot th thead tr ul'.split())
+_BOOL = set('allowfullscreen async autofocus autoplay checked controls default defer disabled formnovalidate hidden inert ismap itemscope loop multiple muted nomodule novalidate open playsinline readonly required reversed selected'.split())
+
+def _opt(options, name):
+    return bool(options.get(name, options.get(name.replace('-', '_'), False)))
+
+def _attrs(raw, keep_quotes, keep_defaults):
+    out=[]
+    for m in _ATTR.finditer(raw):
+        name=m.group(1).lower()
+        value=m.group(2) if m.group(2) is not None else m.group(3) if m.group(3) is not None else m.group(4)
+        if value is None:
+            out.append(' '+name); continue
+        value=html.unescape(value)
+        if not keep_defaults and ((name=='type' and value.lower() in ('text/javascript','application/javascript') ) or (name=='type' and value.lower()=='text/css' and False)):
+            continue
+        if name in _BOOL and value.lower()==name:
+            out.append(' '+name); continue
+        if not keep_quotes and value and re.fullmatch(r'[-\w:.]+',value):
+            out.append(' '+name+'='+value)
+        else:
+            quote='"'
+            if not keep_quotes and '"' in value and "'" not in value: quote="'"
+            out.append(' '+name+'='+quote+html.escape(value,quote=True).replace(''', ''')+quote)
+    return ''.join(out)
+
+def minify_html(source, options=None):
+    options=options or {}
+    keep_doc=_opt(options,'html-keep-document-tags')
+    keep_end=_opt(options,'html-keep-end-tags')
+    keep_ws=_opt(options,'html-keep-whitespace')
+    keep_comments=_opt(options,'html-keep-comments')
+    keep_special=_opt(options,'html-keep-special-comments') or _opt(options,'html-keep-conditional-comments')
+    keep_quotes=_opt(options,'html-keep-quotes')
+    keep_defaults=_opt(options,'html-keep-default-attrvals')
+    tokens=_TOKEN.findall(source)
+    out=[]; pending=''; prev_tag=''; raw_tag=''
+    for tok in tokens:
+        if raw_tag:
+            end=re.search(r'</\s*'+raw_tag+r'\s*>',tok,re.I)
+            if end:
+                body=tok[:end.start()]
+                if raw_tag=='style':
+                    try:
+                        from css_min import minify_css
+                        body=minify_css(body)
+                    except Exception: body=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',body).strip()
+                elif raw_tag=='script':
+                    try:
+                        from jsmin import minify_js
+                        body=minify_js(body)
+                    except Exception: body=body.strip()
+                out.append(body); tok=tok[end.start():]; raw_tag=''
+            else:
+                out.append(tok); continue
+        if tok.startswith('<!--'):
+            special=bool(re.match(r'<!--\s*(?:\[if|#)',tok,re.I))
+            if keep_comments or (special and keep_special): out.append(tok)
+            continue
+        if tok.startswith('<!'):
+            if tok.lower().startswith('<!doctype'):
+                out.append('<!doctype html>')
+            elif keep_comments: out.append(tok)
+            continue
+        if tok.startswith('</'):
+            m=re.match(r'</\s*([\w:-]+)',tok)
+            if not m: continue
+            tag=m.group(1).lower()
+            if not keep_doc and tag in ('html','head','body'): continue
+            if not keep_end and tag in ('p','li','dt','dd','option','thead','tbody','tfoot','tr','td','th','colgroup'): continue
+            if pending:
+                if keep_ws or (prev_tag not in _BLOCK and tag not in _BLOCK): out.append('\n' if '\n' in pending else ' ')
+                pending=''
+            out.append('</'+tag+'>'); prev_tag=tag
+            continue
+        if tok.startswith('<'):
+            m=re.match(r'<\s*([\w:-]+)([\s\S]*?)>',tok)
+            if not m:
+                out.append(tok); continue
+            tag=m.group(1).lower(); tail=m.group(2)
+            if not keep_doc and tag in ('html','head','body'):
+                prev_tag=tag; continue
+            if pending:
+                if keep_ws or (prev_tag not in _BLOCK and tag not in _BLOCK): out.append('\n' if '\n' in pending else ' ')
+                pending=''
+            attrs=_attrs(tail,keep_quotes,keep_defaults)
+            out.append('<'+tag+attrs+('>' if tag in _VOID else '>'))
+            prev_tag=tag
+            if tag in ('script','style'): raw_tag=tag
+            continue
+        # text node
+        if tok.isspace():
+            pending+=tok; continue
+        text=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',tok)
+        if pending:
+            if keep_ws or (prev_tag not in _BLOCK): out.append('\n' if '\n' in pending else ' ')
+            pending=''
+        if not keep_ws:
+            text=text.strip()
+        out.append(text)
+        prev_tag=''
+    result=''.join(out)
+    # A trailing text whitespace before a closing block is insignificant.
+    return result.strip()
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r);

"""Small standalone CSS minifier used by the CLI implementation."""
import re


def _comments(s):
    out=[]; i=0; quote=None
    while i<len(s):
        c=s[i]
        if quote:
            out.append(c)
            if c=='\\' and i+1<len(s): i+=1; out.append(s[i])
            elif c==quote: quote=None
            i+=1; continue
        if c in "'\"": quote=c; out.append(c); i+=1; continue
        if s.startswith('/*',i):
            j=s.find('*/',i+2)
            if j<0: break
            comment=s[i:j+2]
            if comment.startswith('/*!'): out.append('/*!'+comment[3:-2].strip()+'*/')
            i=j+2; continue
        out.append(c); i+=1
    return ''.join(out)


def _numbers(s, precision):
    def sub(m):
        n=m.group()
        try:
            v=float(n)
            if precision: v=float(format(v, f'.{precision}g'))
            z=format(v,'.15g')
            if z.startswith('0.'): z=z[1:]
            elif z.startswith('-0.'): z='-'+z[2:]
            return z
        except ValueError: return n
    return re.sub(r'(?<![\w#-])[-+]?(?:\d*\.\d+|\d+\.?\d*)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?',sub,s)


def minify_css(text, precision=0, version=0):
    s=_comments(text)
    # Whitespace can be dropped at punctuation; keep descendant combinators and
    # spaces between identifiers. Strings are protected by the scanner below.
    out=[]; i=0; quote=None; pending=False
    for c in s:
        if quote:
            out.append(c)
            if c==quote: quote=None
            elif c=='\\': pass
            continue
        if c in "'\"":
            if pending and out and (out[-1].isalnum() or out[-1] in '_-'):
                out.append(' ')
            pending=False; quote=c; out.append(c); continue
        if c.isspace():
            # License comments are emitted as self-contained tokens; adjacent
            # selectors need no separator after them.
            if out and out[-1]=='/' and ''.join(out).endswith('*/'): pending=False
            else: pending=True
            continue
        if c in '{}:;,>+~()':
            while out and out[-1]==' ': out.pop()
            out.append(c); pending=False
        else:
            if pending and out and out[-1] not in '{:;,>+~(' and c not in '})],;:': out.append(' ')
            pending=False; out.append(c)
    s=''.join(out)
    s=re.sub(r';}', '}',s)
    s=re.sub(r'\s*!\s*', '!', s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(font-weight\s*:\s*)bold\b',r'\g<1>700',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(font-weight\s*:\s*)normal\b',r'\g<1>400',s)
    # Canonicalize common legacy color functions and named colors.
    def rgb(m):
        try:
            vals=[int(x.strip()) for x in m.group(1).split(',')]
            if len(vals)==3 and all(0<=x<=255 for x in vals):
                h=''.join('%02x'%x for x in vals)
                if h[0]==h[1] and h[2]==h[3] and h[4]==h[5]: h=h[0]+h[2]+h[4]
                return '#'+h
        except Exception: pass
        return m.group(0)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)rgba\(\s*([\d\s,]+)\s*,\s*1(?:\.0+)?\s*\)',lambda m:'rgb('+m.group(1)+')',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)rgb\(\s*([\d\s,]+)\s*\)',rgb,s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)hsl\(\s*0\s*,\s*100%\s*,\s*50%\s*\)', 'red', s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)rgba\(\s*0\s*,\s*0\s*,\s*0\s*,\s*0(?:\.0+)?\s*\)', 'transparent', s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(?:margin|padding|border-width)\s*:\s*([^;}]+)',lambda m:m.group(0),s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?<![\w.])(?:0)(?:px|em|rem|%|pt|cm|mm|in|pc|ex|ch|vh|vw)\b','0',s,flags=re.I)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#([0-9a-f])\1([0-9a-f])\2([0-9a-f])\3\b',r'#\1\2\3',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ff0000\b','red',s); s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ffffff\b','#fff',s); s=re.sub(r'(?i)#000000\b','#000',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#f00\b','red',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#808080\b','gray',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)#ffff00\b','#ff0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\byellow\b','#ff0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\bwhite\b','#fff',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(background(?:-image)?):(?:none|transparent)(?=[;}])',r'\1:0 0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(background-color):transparent(?=[;}])',r'\1:initial',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(border):0(?:px)?\s+none(?=[;}])',r'\1:0',s)
    s=re.sub(r'@import\s+url\((['+"'\""+r'])([^()]*?)\1\)\s*;?',lambda m:'@import '+m.group(1)+m.group(2)+m.group(1),s,flags=re.I)
    # Font family names are case-insensitive and quote-free when safe.
    def fonts(m):
        vals=[]
        for v in m.group(1).split(','):
            v=v.strip()
            if len(v)>1 and v[0] in "'\"" and v[-1]==v[0]:
                v=v[1:-1].lower()
            vals.append(v)
        return 'font-family:'+','.join(vals)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)font-family:([^;}]+)',fonts,s)
    s=re.sub(r'url\((['+"'\""+r'])([^()]*?)\1\)',lambda m:'url('+m.group(2)+')' if re.fullmatch(r'[\w./#:%+-]+',m.group(2)) else m.group(0),s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:[^;}]*?)\bnormal\b',r'\g<1>',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:[^;}]*?)\bbold\b',r'\g<1>700',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:)[ \t]+',r'\1',s)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)(font:[^;}]*?)\s{2,}',r'\1 ',s)
    s=_numbers(s,precision)
    # CSS calc's binary plus operator requires separating whitespace.
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)calc\(([^()]*)\)',lambda m:'calc('+re.sub(r'(?<=\S)\+(?=\S)',' + ',m.group(1))+')',s)
    # Four-value shorthand reductions.
    def shorthand(m):
        p=m.group(1); vals=m.group(2).split()
        if len(vals)==4 and vals[3]==vals[1]: vals.pop()
        if len(vals)==3 and vals[0]==vals[2]: vals.pop()
        if len(vals)==2 and vals[0]==vals[1]: vals.pop()
        return p+':'+ ' '.join(vals)
    s=re.sub(r'(?i)\b(margin|padding|border-width):([^;}]+)',shorthand,s)
    s=re.sub(r';+$','',s)
    return s

"""Conservative JavaScript tokenizer/minifier used by the CLI implementation."""
import re

_TOKEN = re.compile(r'''\s+|//[^\r\n]*|/\*[\s\S]*?\*/|(?:'(?:\\.|[^'\\])*'|"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|`(?:\\.|[^`\\])*`)|(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)|(?:[$\w]+)|(?:===|!==|>>>|==|!=|<=|>=|=>|\+\+|--|&&|\|\||\?\?|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|\*\*|\.\.\.|<<|>>)''')
_WORD = re.compile(r'^[\w$]')

def minify_js(source, options=None):
    options = options or {}
    def opt(name, default=None):
        return options.get(name, options.get(name.replace('-', '_'), default))
    tokens = []
    pos = 0
    while pos < len(source):
        m = _TOKEN.match(source, pos)
        if not m:
            tokens.append(source[pos]); pos += 1; continue
        t = m.group(0); pos = m.end()
        if t.isspace() or t.startswith('//') or (t.startswith('/*') and not t.startswith('/*!')):
            continue
        if t in ('true', 'false'):
            nxt=source[pos:].lstrip()
            prev=tokens[-1] if tokens else ''
            is_key=(prev in ('.','?.') or (prev in ('{',',') and (nxt.startswith(':') or nxt.startswith('('))))
            if not is_key:
                t='!0' if t=='true' else '!1'
        elif re.fullmatch(r'\d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?', t):
            precision = int(opt('js-precision', 0) or 0)
            if precision:
                try:
                    t = format(float(t), f'.{precision}g')
                    t = re.sub(r'e([+-])0+(\d+)', r'e\1\2', t)
                except (ValueError, OverflowError):
                    pass
        tokens.append(t)
    # Concatenate adjacent plain string literals when doing so is unambiguous.
    i = 0
    while i + 2 < len(tokens):
        a, op, b = tokens[i:i+3]
        if (op == '+' and len(a) >= 2 and len(b) >= 2 and a[0] == a[-1] and b[0] == b[-1]
                and a[0] in "'\"" and b[0] in "'\""
                and not any(c in a[1:-1] + b[1:-1] for c in ('\\', a[0], b[0]))):
            tokens[i:i+3] = [a[0] + a[1:-1] + b[1:-1] + a[0]]
        else:
            i += 1
    # Join simple adjacent declarations of the same kind.
    ident = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$')
    atom = re.compile(r'^(?:[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*|\d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?|!0|!1|true|false|null|undefined|(?:\"[^\"\\]*\"|\'[^\'\\]*\'))$')
    i = 0
    while i + 8 < len(tokens):
        kind = tokens[i]
        if (kind in ('let', 'var', 'const') and ident.fullmatch(tokens[i+1]) and tokens[i+2] == '='
                and atom.fullmatch(tokens[i+3]) and tokens[i+4] == ';' and tokens[i+5] == kind
                and ident.fullmatch(tokens[i+6]) and tokens[i+7] == '=' and atom.fullmatch(tokens[i+8])
                and (i+9 == len(tokens) or tokens[i+9] == ';')):
            stop=i+10 if i+9 < len(tokens) else i+9
            tokens[i:stop] = [kind, tokens[i+1], '=', tokens[i+3], ',', tokens[i+6], '=', tokens[i+8], ';']
        else:
            i += 1
    # Turn a guarded pair of single call statements into a conditional expression.
    def close_at(seq, start, left, right):
        depth=0
        for j in range(start, len(seq)):
            if seq[j] == left: depth += 1
            elif seq[j] == right:
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0: return j
        return -1
    def call_stmt(seq):
        if not seq: return False
        depth=0; saw_call=False
        for j,t in enumerate(seq):
            if t == '(': depth+=1; saw_call=True
            elif t == ')':
                depth-=1
                if depth<0:return False
            elif t in ('{','}',';'):
                return t==';' and j==len(seq)-1 and depth==0 and saw_call
        return depth==0 and saw_call
    i=0
    while i < len(tokens):
        if tokens[i] != 'if' or i+1>=len(tokens) or tokens[i+1] != '(':
            i+=1; continue
        cp=close_at(tokens,i+1,'(',')')
        if cp<0 or cp+1>=len(tokens) or tokens[cp+1]!='{': i+=1; continue
        b1=close_at(tokens,cp+1,'{','}')
        if b1<0: i+=1; continue
        cond=tokens[i+2:cp]; yes=tokens[cp+2:b1]
        if b1+1>=len(tokens) or tokens[b1+1]!='else' or b1+2>=len(tokens) or tokens[b1+2]!='{':
            if yes and yes[0] in ('return','var','let','const'):
                tokens[i:b1+1]=['if']+tokens[i+1:cp+1]+yes
                i=max(0,i-1)
            else: i+=1
            continue
        b2=close_at(tokens,b1+2,'{','}')
        if b2<0: i+=1; continue
        no=tokens[b1+3:b2]
        if yes and no and yes[0]=='return' and no[0]=='return' and cond:
            y=yes[1:-1] if yes[-1:]==[';'] else yes[1:]
            n=no[1:-1] if no[-1:]==[';'] else no[1:]
            tokens[i:b2+1]=['return']+cond+['?']+y+[':']+n+[';']
            i=max(0,i-1)
        elif call_stmt(yes) and call_stmt(no) and cond:
            if yes[-1:]==[';']: yes=yes[:-1]
            if no[-1:]==[';']: no=no[:-1]
            tokens[i:b2+1]=cond+['?']+yes+[':']+no
            i=max(0,i-1)
        else: i+=1
    out = ''
    prev = ''
    for t in tokens:
        if prev and ((_WORD.match(prev[-1:]) and _WORD.match(t[:1])) or (prev[-1:] in '+-' and t[:1] == prev[-1:]) or (prev[-1:] == '/' and t.startswith('/'))):
            out += ' '
        out += t
        prev = t
    # Safe punctuation cleanup: remove semicolons immediately before a closing brace.
    out = re.sub(r';+}', '}', out)
    # Collapse simple conditional expression statements.
    ternary = re.compile(r'\bif\(([^(){}]+)\)\{([^{};]+)\}else\{([^{};]+)\}')
    def ternary_expr(m):
        if re.match(r'(?:return|throw|break|continue|var|let|const)\b', m.group(2)) or re.match(r'(?:return|throw|break|continue|var|let|const)\b', m.group(3)):
            return m.group(0)
        return m.group(1)+'?'+m.group(2)+':'+m.group(3)
    out = ternary.sub(ternary_expr, out)
    guarded = re.compile(r'\bif\(([^(){}]+)\)\{([^{}]+)\}(?!\s*else)')
    def guarded_expr(m):
        statements=[x for x in m.group(2).split(';') if x]
        if not statements or any(re.match(r'(?:return|throw|break|continue|var|let|const)\b', x) for x in statements):
            return m.group(0)
        expr=statements[0] if len(statements)==1 else '('+','.join(statements)+')'
        return m.group(1)+'&&'+expr
    out = guarded.sub(guarded_expr, out)
    # Remove a final semicolon (the parser's output convention).
    out = re.sub(r';+$', '', out)
    return out
